Do you know any games that have great gameplay mechanics but bad level design? Or bad gameplay mechanics but great level design?

Hmm... for the first one I think I'll go for Devil May Cry 4: wonderful gameplay but boring and repetitive levels that then it makes you replay. I think you could say that the original Dark Souls had a noticeable drop in the quality of its last levels. (I'm looking at you Izalith)

More recently I think Destiny fits (or at least it used to), with its brilliant gameplay and downright limited and repetitive "levels". Also, you could mention some mobile games that do have (surprisingly!) entertaining mechanics that are ruined by the conventions of the genre.

Now on the bad gameplay but good level design... that one is hard, a game with bad gameplay is hardly worth playing (so good level design goes unnoticed or wasted), much less remembering. Still, I think I remember saying something like that about some parts of Xenosaga 2.

This might be an unpopular opinion but the whole Elder Scroll series has fantastic "levels" but doesn't give you much to do but going from point A to point B and back, fighting bad AI monsters by repeatedly clicking a button, and collecting a huge variety of items. I loved Morrowind's world, but I hated living in it.

I thought draugr were pretty cool (they are essentially norse mummies) at first but once I realized that almost EVERY SINGLE QUEST is just "go into the dungeon, kill the draugr and/or bandits and grab mcguffin" I lost most of my enjoyment, it actually got to the point where i'd rather see skeletons (aka one of the most generic RPG enemies after goblins, bandits, and wolves) than draugr because at least it was something new.

Even though Oblivion had a lot more standard fantasy monsters (skeletons, goblins, minotaurs, ogres) I never got bored of them because at least I would be doing 5 dungeons of the same monster in a row and it occasionally had some weirder monsters thrown in (anyone remember Dreughs?). And now I'm reminded of one of the things that really saddened me about skyrim , that they removed a lot of really cool monsters and especially Daedra like Clannfears, Spider Daedra (ok they were really just driders but still) and Daedroths. Instead for daedra we just get elementals(atronachs) and demons(dremora). I guess it just wasn't worth the time to bother modeling them when they'd have be so rare (since the oblivion crises is over) but It would have at least added a little more variety than just dozens of Draugr dungeons, like 3 or 4 vampire dens, and bandits.

I find myself with an issue with their dungeons. I don't like curvy but linear like they tend to be, but when I start going in circles as there is no path or way to tell where I have been from where I need to go I get annoyed with being lost in what is now empty space.

Great level design but bad mechanics: doom II.

But install Brutal Doom and now it's a modern first person shooter that puts most modern games to shame.
I would say Doom had a bit dodgy level design because I somehow managed to get lost. I'm also not the fan of damaging floors. You know, when I happen to have just a few hitpoints.

I guess I could put Planetside 2 on both sides of the equation. Pretty good level design for many bases, but terrible environment design for the main conflict hubs. Gameplay starts out fun, but quickly hits the money wall and it killed the experience. I put around $60 into that F2P game and played around 100 hours. Most of the weapons I bought were either nerfed to shit or just moderate upgrades. The primary thing that made me quit was that not only do your upgrades not transfer faction to faction, but they do not transfer server to server.

Whoever at SOE made the "business decisions" for PlanetSide dug their own grave and seriously contributed to the death of their studio.
